title: District Commission's Obligation to Give Opportunity of Being Heard

content.scenario: A consumer, Kumar, files a complaint with the District Commission against a service provider for deficient service. The Commission decides to reject the complaint.
content.outcome: The District Commission must give the complainant (Kumar) an opportunity of being heard before rejecting the complaint, as per section 36(2) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and the admissibility of the complaint shall ordinarily be decided within 21 days from the date on which the complaint was filed.

user_queries: What is the procedure for rejecting a complaint by the District Commission?
Can the District Commission reject a complaint without giving the complainant an opportunity of being heard?
What is the time limit for the District Commission to decide on the admissibility of a complaint?
